facts.text: At any tool-chain cost level, a multi-fidelity hierarchy is more defensible than testing every combination of snow, dust, glare, 100 sites, every sensor and particle soil at maximum fidelity.
facts.quote: Whatever the cost level, a multi-fidelity hierarchy is more defensible than running every combination of snow, dust, glare, 100 sites, every sensor and particle soil at maximum fidelity. **Expert opinion**.

facts.text: The multi-fidelity test architecture uses deterministic functional and object-list tests for millions of braking-logic combinations.
facts.quote: Deterministic functional and object-list tests for millions of braking-logic combinations.

facts.text: The multi-fidelity test architecture uses medium-fidelity closed-loop dynamics with ideal or noisy sensors for broad regression testing.
facts.quote: Medium-fidelity closed-loop dynamics with ideal or noisy sensors for broad regression.

facts.text: The multi-fidelity test architecture reserves high-fidelity rendering, radar and lidar for perception-sensitive subsets of test cases.
facts.quote: High-fidelity rendering, radar and lidar for perception-sensitive subsets.

facts.text: The multi-fidelity test architecture reserves high-fidelity soil or DEM for braking- and traction-sensitive subsets of test cases.
facts.quote: High-fidelity soil or DEM for braking- and traction-sensitive subsets.

facts.text: The multi-fidelity test architecture uses hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing for timing, ECU and interface behavior.
facts.quote: HIL for timing, ECU and interface behavior.

facts.text: The multi-fidelity test architecture uses targeted physical tests for correlation and final evidence.
facts.quote: Targeted physical tests for correlation and final evidence.

facts.text: Allocation of test cases to each level of the multi-fidelity hierarchy must be based on sensitivity and correlation work, not assumptions.
facts.quote: The allocation of cases to each level must come from sensitivity and correlation work, not from assumption.
